meta.title: Why Hobbes says life without rules is nasty, brutish, and short

plates.want: Bruegel, war of all against all (PD)

beats.text: Imagine no government, no police, no law. Total freedom. Hobbes said it would be hell.
With no power to keep order, every person becomes a threat to every other person.
No trust, no trade, no building for a future that any rival might simply take.
He called it the war of all against all, and life inside it: "solitary, poor, nasty, brutish, and short."
So, he argued, we strike a bargain. We each surrender some freedom to a common power.
That power is the Leviathan — a sovereign strong enough to frighten us all into peace.
Every rule you resent, Hobbes would say, is the price of not living in that endless war.
